analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: Establishing a Foothold
key_insights: GS sees tactical value in fading the latest phase of 10y UST underperformance and recommends receiving 10s on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly (entry 2bp, target -4bp, stop 6bp). Valuation, positioning and lower convexity risk support asymmetry toward lower yields.
Longer-term forwards are elevated versus fair value for most G10 markets, which supports the case for duration at these levels.
Recent credit spread pressure showed clearer cracks in markets' ability to absorb a high-vol selloff without tighter financial conditions, most notably in Europe.

US positioning now points to an investor base better hedged against a further yield rise. Total return bond funds are growing underweight versus benchmark, and asset managers cut long-end futures duration by $40-45bn 10y equivalents since the start of September.

MBS index duration rose 0.3-0.4y since the start of September, worth about $60bn in 10y-equivalent paying needs. MBS convexity is now close to zero, so further yield moves should not generate meaningful additional convexity paying.
10s underperformance on the fly mainly reflects directionality with yield levels. Empirically, 10s underperform more in selloffs that come with a large MBS duration extension, as happened recently.

Spillovers from abroad onto 10y USTs have turned from bearish to bullish since mid-September. Thursday's rate rally came despite higher energy prices, which GS reads partly as sensitivity to news that shakes confidence in the AI trade.

Limited evidence of concentrated foreign UST selling. NY Fed custody holdings fell in step with Dollar strength, which fits FX intervention rather than active selling. TIC data through July and Japan data through August show no material unwinds.

Implied vol remains elevated across the surface. Given the premium on protecting against higher yields versus lower, GS sees value in selling payers outright or risk reversals on 1-2y expiries and 2-5y tails.
Market function stress is limited. Depth declines were modest, price impact of order flow is stable, and cost-to-sweep rose less than in April 2025.

GS is bullish on Bunds and keeps its 10y Bund forecast at 3.25% at end-2026. Energy upside is translating into curve flattening, sovereign stress is producing a safe-haven bid, and tighter euro area financing could challenge growth sentiment.

OATs stabilized this week but spreads remain near the wides. GS attributes the widening mainly to higher rates vol and lower vol-adjusted carry rather than Japanese selling, and expects OATs to stabilise tighter, contingent on lower core rates and vol.

BTPs have widened more against Bunds than energy and vol betas imply, yet they outperform OATs, which suggests little political risk premium. The government revised 2027 and 2028 deficit targets by 1.2ppt of GDP cumulatively. GS sees better risk-reward in Bonos.

Gilts: BoE communication has been hawkish (Greene, Pill) and the September MPC opened the door to tightening, so front-end rallies should stay limited. Limiting near-term fiscal slippage is needed to prevent a rise in Gilt risk premium ahead of the 28 October budget. Net Gilt supply to the private sector should decline, helped by a friendlier BoE QT profile.
GS economists expect the upcoming US CPI release to be boosted by higher energy and other commodity costs and seasonal distortions.

GS expects Bund yields to fall, with asymmetry building toward longs.

risk_factors: Energy prices, particularly refined products and distant crude forwards, still heavily influence day-to-day bond performance.
Elevated implied vol keeps rate hedges expensive.
Further French political risk or rising Italian political risk.
Fiscal slippage ahead of the UK budget could raise Gilt risk premium.
Upcoming CPI release boosted by energy and seasonal distortions.
Possible remaining unhedged MBS risk that would look like a duration unwind.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuation, hedged positioning, near-zero MBS convexity and bullish foreign spillovers argue for lower yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy risks have not subsided, implied vol is elevated, belly yields are near the top of their range, and upcoming CPI is expected to be boosted by energy and seasonal factors.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The trade stop at 6bp on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly.

tension_points.bull_case: Widening has outstripped fundamental drivers, so OATs should stabilise tighter.
tension_points.bear_case: Spreads remain near the wides and French political risk persists.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A lack of support from lower core rates and rates volatility, or no improvement in the domestic macro outlook.
